items.title: US bans BYD from air base in Japan over security concern
items.summary: SEOUL: The US armed forces have banned Chinese carmaker BYD's electric vehicles from an air base in Japan over security concerns, South Korea's Yonhap news agency reported on Friday, after Washington added the company to a list of enterprises it believes are aiding China's military. The concern stems from the use of cameras and sensors mounted on the vehicles, which the US believes could collect and leak sensitive security-related information from the base, Yonhap reported, citing US military officials stationed in Japan. US military officials in Japan could not immediately be reached for confirmation.

items.title: Teen, 13, allegedly knifes 69-year-old man in Kanowit public toilet
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 23 — A 69-year-old man was injured in the shoulder after he was allegedly attacked with a knife by a 13-year-old boy at a public toilet in Kanowit, Sarawak, yesterday. Sinar Harian reported Kanowit district police chief DSP Junical Ujal as saying police received a report of the incident at 3.29pm. “According to the call, a 13-year-old boy was reported to have injured a man using a knife.

items.title: Zetrix AI misses D-Day on RM2bil sukuk breach, default risk looms
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Zetrix AI Bhd seems to have missed Thursday's deadline to resolve a covenant breach under its RM2 billion sukuk programme. As of press time, Zetrix AI had not issued any statement on whether it had secured a waiver from sukukholders or reached an agreement with the sukuk trustee. Without a resolution, the digital services and blockchain group faces potential repayment obligations of RM2.16 billion, comprising RM2 billion in principal and RM164.5 million in future coupon payments.

items.title: Japan's core inflation exceeds BoJ target, cements near-term rate hike chance
items.summary: TOKYO: Japan's core consumer inflation exceeded the central bank's two per cent target in September for the first time in nine months, data showed on Friday, a sign of broadening price pressure that cements the case for a near-term interest rate hike. The core consumer price index, which excludes volatile fresh food but includes fuel costs, rose 2.1 per cent in September from a year earlier, data showed, matching a median market forecast and accelerating from a 1.7 per cent rise in August. In a sign of broadening inflationary pressure, goods prices rose 2.8 per cent year-on-year in September, accelerating from a 2.6 per cent gain in August, the data showed.

items.title: Eight Thais held for running tomyam businesses on visit passes
items.summary: BALIK PULAU: Eight Thai citizens were arrested for allegedly operating tomyam eateries using social visit passes and border passes during an integrated operation in Balik Pulau. Penang Immigration director Syamsul Fitry Ahmad said the operation, which ended at 1am, targeted foreign-run businesses, particularly those operated by Thais. "Some of them were using social visit passes and border passes," he said.

items.title: Ismail Lasim denies reports he will resign as Negri Sembilan MB
items.summary: SEREMBAN: Negri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim has denied reports that he will resign soon to make way for someone else amid the ongoing constitutional crisis in the state. Ismail, who is also the Juasseh assemblyman, described the claim circulating on social media as merely "political games" by certain quarters. Ismail's press secretary, Mohd Fasha Musthafa, also denied the report, describing it as untrue.

items.title: Anwar vows Malaysia’s support for peace and stability in southern Thailand
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 23 — Malaysia is committed to playing a constructive role in supporting efforts to achieve regional peace and stability, including in southern Thailand, says Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. He said dialogue based on trust, mutual understanding and openness was crucial to paving the way for a comprehensive and lasting peaceful solution for the wellbeing of the people in southern Thailand. Anwar said this in a Facebook post last night after receiving a courtesy call from Malaysia’s Facilitator for the Southern Thailand Peace Dialogue Process, Lt Gen (Rtd) Datuk Ahmad Norihan Jalal, who was recently appointed to the post.

items.title: Aunty Elen's story highlights the strength of Malaysia's neighbourly ties [WATCH]
items.summary: MELAKA: For longtime Duyong resident Aunty Elen, decades of friendship with neighbours of different races have grown into close bonds built on shared experiences, trust and mutual support. Duyong assemblyman Mohd Noor Helmy shared her story in a video posted on social media. In the video, Aunty Elen recalls fond memories with her friends, from sharing meals and secrets to making up after disagreements.

items.title: 1MDB debt in 2026: RM42.5b paid, but RM20.1b still remains
items.summary: According to the Ministry of Finance (MOF), this figure accounts for the government’s total financial obligations related to 1MDB — amounting to RM51.4 billion — after deducting recovered funds and assets totalling RM31.3 billion. The ministry said the outstanding commitment for government-guaranteed Islamic medium-term notes (IMTN) amounts to RM8.9 billion, comprising RM5 billion in principal and RM3.9 billion in interest, lasting until the maturity date in 2039. Regarding efforts to recover funds, the MOF affirmed that the government remains committed to pursuing claims and asset recovery efforts related to 1MDB.

items.title: Islamic preacher Ustaz Wadi Annuar believed among victims in Gerik three-vehicle crash
items.summary: The 2.40am accident involved a Perodua Myvi, a Toyota Vellfire, and a Perodua Bezza, leaving five people injured, while five others escaped unhurt. Perak Fire and Rescue Department Operations Division assistant director Sabarodzi Nor Ahmad said the department received an emergency call via the NG999 system before dispatching a team from the Gerik station to the scene. "The Myvi driver and two injured occupants of the Vellfire had also been taken to Gerik Hospital by Health Ministry ambulances before the team arrived," he said.

items.title: Taiping council denies Osaka zoo elephants abused, says head swaying and musth normal in captivity
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 23 — The Taiping Municipal Council (MPT) has rejected claims that the three Malaysian elephants sent to Japan’s Tennoji Zoo in Osaka are being abused or neglected, insisting the animals are healthy and have settled into their new surroundings. He was responding to concerns raised on social media that the elephants were displaying behaviour such as head swaying, zoochosis and frequent musth episodes. “Head swaying is also a typical behaviour when elephants anticipate food.

items.title: Ringgit opens higher as AI investment concerns weigh on greenback
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit opened higher on Friday as the greenback weakened after equity prices fell amid heightened concern over artificial intelligence (AI)-related investments. At 8am, the ringgit rose to 4.0785/0855 against the greenback from Thursday's close of 4.0815/0850. Mohd Afzanizam added that the US Dollar Index eased 0.15 per cent to 101.625 points.

items.title: #NSTviral: Man cradling two baby crocodiles fascinates netizens
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Two baby crocodiles, an unusual lullaby and a man rocking the reptiles to sleep — hardly an everyday naptime scene. That was what greeted Threads users in a viral video posted by bedamau_bro, showing a man cradling one crocodile in his arms while another rested on his lap at an amusement park in Selayang. The reptiles even have names — Ali and Ahcong — as the user revealed in the comments while inviting visitors to meet them.

items.title: Fadhlina: Budget 2027 to drive new curriculum and Malaysia Education Plan
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 22 — The Ministry of Education (MOE) will focus on rolling out the new curriculum and the Malaysia Education Plan 2026-2035 next year, using the 2027 Budget allocation to drive improvements in the quality of education. “This allocation enables us to implement the Malaysia Education Plan 2026-2035, particularly next year’s key focus, the new curriculum. Fadhlina said the 2027 Budget also prioritised easing schooling costs for families through various aid and allowances, including the Form Six allowance, Early Schooling Aid (BAP), the allowance for Students with Special Educational Needs and incentives for special education teachers.

items.title: Oil tanker rate spike: Gains for some, pain for others [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Surging oil tanker rates amid the Middle East conflict could raise operating costs for Malaysia's oil and gas (O&G) industry, although economists said upstream producers and tanker operators may benefit from higher crude prices and charter rates. These disruptions have lengthened delivery times and reduced fleet efficiency, pushing freight rates higher. Rising transportation and insurance costs could squeeze refining margins, increase fuel subsidy requirements and raise business operating costs.

items.title: 16 areas record unhealthy API readings, Johan Setia highest at 161
items.summary: Melaka's Bukit Rambai and Batu Pahat in Johor recorded readings of 151, while Tangkak recorded 141. In Sarawak, Sri Aman recorded an unhealthy reading of 151. Terengganu's Paka recorded 78, while Kuala Terengganu and Besut recorded 57 and 56 respectively.

items.title: Penang hit-and-run: SUV driver arrested after killing two on expressway
items.summary: Timur Laut police chief ACP Abdul Rozak Muhammad said the 23-year-old man, who was driving a sport utility vehicle (SUV), was arrested at 1 pm after turning himself in at the Timur Laut District Police Headquarters (IPD) here. Abdul Rozak said police would apply for a remand order today to facilitate further investigations. Abdul Rozak said post-mortem examinations found that the male motorcyclist died from severe head and neck injuries, while the woman died from severe head injuries.

items.title: The ones who get it done
items.summary: Why do some employees seem to carry a heavier burden than others, often becoming the first people approached when deadlines loom, problems arise or expectations are not being met? They make things happen. Employees who consistently deliver reduce that uncertainty.

items.title: Indonesia records over 333,000 acute respiratory infection cases as fires rage
items.summary: ISTANBUL: Indonesia has recorded 333,470 cases of acute respiratory infections (ARIs) linked to forest and land fires in several regions, the Health Ministry said on Thursday. The ministry's director of environmental health, Then Suyanti, said daily cases remained high, with 4,522 new cases reported, Anadolu Ajansi reported, citing state-run news agency Antara. She said the latest Air Pollutant Index showed that air quality in several areas had reached hazardous levels, particularly in six provinces prioritised for fire management: Riau, Jambi, South Sumatra, West Kalimantan, South Kalimantan and Central Kalimantan.

items.title: At least 16 dead in Tibet quake
items.summary: BEIJING: At least 16 people were killed and 32 others injured when a powerful 7.0-magnitude earthquake struck China's remote Tibet region, state news agency Xinhua reported, citing local authorities. Officials were still assessing the damage, and disaster relief work was ongoing, Xinhua said. A level-II earthquake disaster emergency response was activated in the area, Xinhua said.

items.title: New York votes to ban Central Park horse carriages after decades of debate
items.summary: NEW YORK: New York's City Council on Thursday voted to ban horse-drawn carriages in Central Park, signalling the end of a tourist ritual that has been the subject of heated debate for years. If the mayor signs it, the ban will take effect in June 2028. The lead-up period is intended to help the approximately 150 active carriage drivers find new employment, City Council Speaker Julie Menin told journalists ahead of the vote.

items.title: KLIA emerges as key airport for smuggling young gibbons
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Young gibbons are being hidden in suitcases and smuggled on passenger flights, with Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) the most frequently implicated airport in a new study. The wildlife trade monitoring organisation Traffic recorded at least 86 gibbons intercepted in 33 airport smuggling incidents linked to Southeast Asia between January 2024 and last August. KLIA was linked to 16 cases involving at least 54 gibbons, including 32 seized at the airport.

items.title: Taiwan shuts down ahead of weakening Typhoon Champi, hundreds of flights cancelled
items.summary: At one point a super typhoon and one of the strongest storms in the Pacific this year, Champi was still packing gusts of around 191kph near its centre, according to Taiwan's Central Weather Administration (CWA). The storm was about 330km (205 miles) east of Taiwan's southern tip, the CWA said. The administration said its radius was around 320km, large enough to cover most of Taiwan, and weather experts said its impact could last nearly two days.

items.title: US judge orders Trump to testify in BBC defamation case by Dec 11
items.summary: MIAMI: A US judge on Thursday set a Dec 11 deadline for President Donald Trump to testify under oath in his US$10 billion defamation lawsuit against the BBC. If Trump fails to attend the deposition by the deadline, he risks sanctions, including dismissal of his lawsuit, the court said. Trump filed his lawsuit against the BBC in December 2025 and is seeking at least US$5 billion on each of two counts.

items.title: NUTP: Teachers lack training to detect violent behaviour among students
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Teachers are not trained to spot or handle aggressive and extremist behaviour among schoolchildren, as they can only rely on the discipline guidebook to address issues, said the National Union of the Teaching Profession (NUTP). NUTP secretary-general Fouzi Singon said current school guidelines do not equip teachers with the skills needed to manage cases of such behaviour. He said without proper training, teachers cannot distinguish violent behaviours and must rely on their own experience.

items.title: Show me the money: A guide to getting the most out of your Budget 2027 financial aid
items.summary: Direct cash transfers: STR and SARA payouts The Rahmah initiatives remain the foundation of the government’s welfare strategy, channelling direct support to lower-income households. Under Budget 2027, Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (SARA) provides up to RM150 a month, capping at RM1,800 annually for Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah (STR) recipients. STR recipients (Monthly SARA) Who qualifies: Approved STR recipients.

items.title: Trump to move forward with planned arch project despite legal action
items.summary: WASHINGTON: Construction of a massive arch in Washington proposed by US President Donald Trump could move ahead despite ongoing legal action, with a recent court filing saying work could begin in two weeks. The proposed giant structure along the Potomac River near Arlington National Cemetery is part of Trump's drive to put his personal stamp on the US capital. In a court filing on Wednesday, the Trump administration said "construction could commence as early as November 5", the same day a commission aligned with Trump is scheduled to vote on approving the project's proposed site and building plans.

items.title: Starshield system is 'back' in Ukraine: Trump
items.summary: WASHINGTON: The Starshield military communications system is "back" in Ukraine, Donald Trump said on Thursday, after The Wall Street Journal reported that the US president had asked tech billionaire Elon Musk to restore the service, which is vital to Kyiv's forces. "I guess the bottom line, he put it back," Trump said, referring to Musk. Musk had previously said that "any limits on speed or usage" of Starshield systems — operated by his SpaceX company — were "decided by the US military and ultimately POTUS", referring to Trump.

items.title: Trump says wind turbine imports threaten national security
items.summary: WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump on Thursday declared imports of wind turbines and their components a threat to national security, but stopped short of imposing new tariffs on the sector. Additional trade measures, including tariffs, could be considered later, the order said. "Given wind energy's intermittent reliability, use of wind energy diverts the United States electrical grid from more reliable energy sources," the order said.

items.title: Around 150,000 rally in Belgrade as Serbia heads to pivotal poll
items.summary: BELGRADE: Around 150,000 supporters of Serbia's opposition student movement rallied in central Belgrade on Thursday, seeking to oust the party of veteran leader Aleksandar Vucic in a pivotal parliamentary election this weekend. The Student List, a leaderless movement of student-backed candidates, wants to end more than 14 years of rule by Vucic's right-wing populist Serbian Progressive Party (SNS) in Sunday's vote. Around 150,000 people gathered at the Student List rally in Belgrade on Thursday evening, according to the independent crowd-monitoring group Archive of Public Gatherings in a post on X.

items.title: Deadly fire at Canada military base was caused by live grenade exercise
items.summary: OTTAWA: A fast-moving grass fire that killed at least four soldiers at a western Canadian military base on Saturday was sparked by an exercise using live grenades, a senior defence official said on Thursday. High winds then propelled the blaze across the army base in Wainwright, overwhelming dozens of soldiers. Officials said 27 people remain hospitalised, several in critical condition.

items.title: Indonesian police link 11 firms to forest, land fires
items.summary: Police have named 11 corporations as suspects in ongoing investigations into forest and land fires, three of which are foreign-invested firms, according to the Antara news agency. National police chief General Suyudi Ario Seto declined to name the companies but said the investigations were proceeding without major obstacles. The report said the criminal proceedings followed an earlier announcement by the National Police's Criminal Investigation Agency, which said it had raised 98 police reports concerning corporate-linked forest fires to the formal investigation stage.

items.title: GOfinance tops 5m users, processes RM3.57b
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: TNG Digital Sdn Bhd's GOfinance platform has recorded more than five million distinct investment users and processed RM3.57 billion in investment value as of Sept 30. TNG Digital chief financial services officer Desmond Teoh said accessibility meant more than lowering minimum investment amounts; users also needed convenient access to a range of investment options. TNG Digital's partnerships have expanded the investment options available through TNG eWallet.

items.title: Public can check 5-day air quality forecasts via MyCMAQ
items.summary: Malaysians can use the Malaysian Community Multiscale Air Quality Model (MyCMAQ) to check air pollution forecasts up to five days ahead. Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Minister Datuk Seri Arthur Joseph Kurup said the system, developed by the Meteorological Department, provided high-resolution forecasts of air quality and atmospheric pollutant concentrations in Malaysia and other parts of Southeast Asia. He added that the 68 automatic air quality monitoring stations operated by the Department of Environment monitored six major air pollutants continuously.

items.title: Govt coordinating efforts to address mental health issues, says Dzulkefly
items.summary: Pressure to achieve academic and career success, relationship problems, social media influence and financial difficulties are among the main factors affecting young people's mental health. Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said the 2023 National Health and Morbidity Survey (NHMS) found that 4.6 per cent of Malaysians aged 16 and above, or about one million people, suffered from depression. In a written parliamentary reply to Datuk Mumtaz Md Nawi (Pas-Tumpat), who asked about the mental well-being of young people, Dzulkefly said his ministry had established the National Centre of Excellence for Mental Health to coordinate government policies and initiatives on mental health.

items.title: Trump ordered to testify under oath in US$10bil BBC lawsuit
items.summary: WASHINGTON: A federal judge on Thursday ordered Donald Trump to sit for a deposition by Dec 11 in his US$10 billion defamation lawsuit against the BBC, which has accused the US president of stalling to avoid answering questions under oath, the Associated Press reported. Trump is suing Britain's publicly funded broadcaster for at least US$10 billion over a misleadingly edited clip of a speech. Trump canceled a deposition in October, citing conflicts with his presidential duties.

items.title: Melaka election: Rauf appointed BN's election director
items.summary: AYER KEROH: Melaka Barisan Nasional chairman Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh has been appointed the coalition's election director for the upcoming state polls. BN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi, in announcing this, said this was because the coalition's election director, deputy chairman Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan was busy with his duties as foreign minister. "So, I proposed (that Rauf takes over as BN's Melaka election director) and the meeting earlier endorsed this... no one else, just him (Rauf)," he said after chairing the BN central committee meeting for the 16th Melaka election.

items.title: Police bust alleged sex trafficking syndicate exploiting children, generating RM450,000 monthly
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 22 — Police have crippled ‘Geng Yunaa’, believed to be involved in 17 cases of child prostitution and trafficking for sexual exploitation, following ‘Ops Angel’ in the Klang Valley from Sept 24 to 26. He said two other group members were already being held at Kajang Prison and Henry Gurney School in Melaka for offences related to child trafficking and prostitution. “The group carried out sexual exploitation through prostitution by recruiting local teenagers, foreign nationals and underage children, who were exploited and made victims of prostitution in Selangor and Kuala Lumpur.

items.title: Viral Porsche road bully jailed five days, fined RM10,000 for dangerous driving
items.summary: PETALING JAYA, Oct 22 — A Porsche Cayenne driver was sentenced to five days in prison and fined RM10,000 by the Magistrate’s Court here today after pleading guilty to dangerous driving of the luxury car on a highway near Bandar Kinrara, which had gone viral on social media. Magistrate Nur Natasya Mohtaruddin, who handed down the sentence against Woo Hong Jiang, 56, ordered the man to serve his prison term starting today, alongside a five-year disqualification of his driving license and six months’ imprisonment if he fails to pay the fine. Deputy Public Prosecutor Adriana Maisarah Mohd Farid requested a heavy sentence, taking into account that dashboard camera (dashcam) footage showed the accused was a road bully who drove dangerously and whose actions could have caused an accident, noting also that the case had gone viral.

items.title: MCMC warns against sharing Kuching school violence footage involving teen, cautions of legal action
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 22 — The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) urges individuals who have uploaded or shared video footage of an incident involving a dangerous weapon at a school in Kuching, Sarawak, to immediately delete the content. The Commission further cautioned that disclosing the identities of children may constitute a violation of Section 15 of the Child Act 2001 (Act 611). “The dissemination of such content may also be subject to action under Section 233 of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998 (Act 588), should it contravene the provisions of the law,” the statement read.

items.title: Samsuri rallies Perikatan machinery for Melaka polls after court freezes RoS deregistration
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 22 — Perikatan Nasional (PN) chairman Datuk Seri Ahmad Samsuri Mokhtar has welcomed a High Court ruling granting an interim stay against the Registrar of Societies’ (RoS) decision to deregister the coalition, saying it will now direct its full electoral machinery towards the Melaka state election. “PN remains steadfast, and this struggle will continue,” he said, offering gratitude to supporters for their prayers and commending the coalition’s legal team for securing the urgent court intervention. Earlier today, High Court Judge Datuk Azizan Md Arshad allowed PN’s leave application to stay the RoS order revoking the coalition’s corporate registration pending the final disposal of its substantive judicial review challenge.

items.title: Anthony Loke backs local transport apps with open data on train schedules, passenger numbers
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 22 — Local application developers can leverage open public transport data to help commuters plan their journeys more conveniently, Transport Minister Anthony Loke said. He said the Transport Ministry (MoT) had adopted an open data policy several years ago, allowing interested parties to access the information to develop public transport applications. “Data under the ministry’s purview mainly relates to public transport, while road-related data involves other agencies, including the Works Ministry and the Public Works Department.

items.title: MACC chief urges MCMC staff to expose misconduct and reject abuse of power
items.summary: Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) Chief Commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman said MCMC staff should have the courage to report any abuse of power or unlawful instructions through official channels. Abd Halim said MCMC’s integrity programmes showed that both its senior management and staff were committed to strengthening accountability. The MCMC 2026 Integrity and Audit Month closing ceremony, themed “Empowering Integrity, Strengthening Governance”, was held at the MCMC Auditorium in Cyberjaya today.

items.title: Two men in viral Bukit Antarabangsa police chase charged with dangerous driving, drugs and weapons offences
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 22 — Two men who went viral on social media after crashing into public vehicles while attempting to evade police in Bukit Antarabangsa were charged in three separate courts in Ampang today on various offences, including obstructing civil servants, possessing dangerous weapons and drugs. Private driver Muhammad Putra Zulfaiz Zaidi, 32, and mechanic Mohamad Danial Haiqal Kamal Arifin, 21, pleaded not guilty to all charges read before Sessions Court Judge Norshila Kamarudin and Magistrates Siti Nur Ain Ariffin and Tiong Wen Wen. Before Judge Norshila Kamarudin, the two friends were jointly charged with possessing dangerous weapons in a public place, namely a machete and a sickle, at Jalan Wangsa 5, Bukit Antarabangsa, at 11 am on Oct 11.

items.title: Police raid Melaka scam call centres targeting Chinese, Vietnamese victims, arrest 29
items.summary: MELAKA, Oct 22 — Police crippled the activities of two call center syndicates suspected of being involved in online non-existent investment scams and love scams through two separate operations around Melaka Raya and Ayer Keroh, here. Melaka Tengah District Police Chief ACP Halim Abas said that in the first operation on October 20, 14 Chinese nationals - comprising 11 men and three women aged between 21 and 52 - were arrested at four accommodation units in a hotel in Melaka Raya between 1pm and 3 pm. “Initial investigations found that the premises were suspected of being used as a call center operations hub for online non-existent investment scam activities targeting Chinese nationals.

items.title: Court of Appeal revokes bail for wheelchair-bound man charged with trafficking 6.2kg of cannabis
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 22 — The Court of Appeal today overturned a High Court decision that had released a wheelchair-bound man on bail pending the disposal of his drug trafficking trial. He held that the High Court judge erred in applying Section 388 of the Criminal Procedure Code to allow bail when there is an express law dealing with bail for drug trafficking offences. The court ordered the RM150,000 bail deposited to be returned and revoked all previously imposed bail conditions.

items.title: Thunderstorms to lash Klang Valley, Penang, and six other states tonight
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 22 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a severe thunderstorm warning, forecasting heavy rain and strong winds across several states and federal territories until 9 pm today. Issued at 5:50 pm, the alert covers the entire Klang Valley, including Kuala Lumpur, Selangor, and Putrajaya, alongside Penang. Meanwhile, Perak is set to take a battering, with alerts plastered across Kerian, Selama, Larut Matang, Manjung, Bagan Datuk, Perak Tengah, Hilir Perak, Kampar, Kinta, and Kuala Kangsar.

items.title: EC opens 30-day review of September 2026 supplementary electoral roll
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 22 — The Supplementary Electoral Roll for September 2026 (DPT BLN9/2026) will be open for review for a period of 30 days, starting today until Nov 20, said Election Commission (EC) secretary Datuk Khairul Shahril Idrus. Additionally, the electoral roll contains 21,720 registered voters who have changed their electoral constituencies, as well as 4,805 voters who have undergone a change in their voter category or status. “The Election Commission (EC) urges citizens aged 18 and above as of the period between September 1 and September 30, 2026 as well as any registered voters who have applied to change their electoral constituency, voter category, or status, to verify their names in the Supplementary Electoral Roll (DPT) for September 2026 (DPT BLN9/2026).

items.title: Remand extended for suspect in AKPS officer’s murder at KLIA quarters
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Oct 22 — The man suspected of murdering his wife, a Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (AKPS) officer, at their residential quarters near Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) in Nilai on Oct 15 has had his remand extended for another seven days. Negeri Sembilan police chief Datuk Alzafny Ahmad said the suspect would remain in remand until Oct 29, while the case was being investigated under Section 302 of the Penal Code. “The extended remand period begins today and runs until Oct 29,” he told reporters.

items.title: Maintain Western technology for DNB, says MP
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 22 — Wawasan information chief and Machang MP Wan Ahmad Fayhsal Wan Ahmad Kamal has urged Putrajaya to maintain Digital Nasional Bhd’s (DNB) Western technology stack, saying it is needed to balance the growing role of Chinese technology in Malaysia’s 5G and AI infrastructure. He said DNB’s Ericsson-based network was now Malaysia’s main Western technology counterweight, following U Mobile’s selection of Huawei for the country’s second 5G network. Wan Fayhsal said Malaysia should not allow one technology ecosystem to become dominant across its critical digital infrastructure.

items.title: Five days’ warning: New Malaysian model forecasts haze before it hits
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 22 — Malaysia will introduce several transformative measures to strengthen efforts to tackle transboundary haze when it chairs the Sub-Regional Ministerial Steering Committee (MSC) on Transboundary Haze Pollution next year. Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Minister Datuk Seri Arthur Joseph Kurup said his ministry was conducting studies and drafting several new initiatives to ensure more effective and concrete action to address the recurring haze problem. “Malaysia will take over the MSC chairmanship next year, and we are studying and planning several new initiatives to strengthen Asean-level efforts to tackle the haze problem.

items.title: No drones without approval, Melaka police tell election candidates
items.summary: MELAKA, Oct 22 — Candidates and political parties intending to use drones during the Melaka State Election campaign must first obtain approval from the relevant authorities and cannot deploy the devices indiscriminately. Melaka police chief Datuk Dzulkhairi Mukhtar said drone operations were subject to regulatory controls by the relevant authorities, including the Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia (CAAM). “Even the police must obtain approval before using drones for operational purposes,” he told reporters after attending a briefing on the 16th Melaka State Election for political party representatives at the Melaka Police Contingent Headquarters here today.

items.title: Snip, snip, slip through? Wire fences cut at illegal crossings near Rantau Panjang-Thai border
items.summary: PASIR MAS, Oct 22 — Eleven police reports regarding damage to concertina wire fences at 13 illegal crossing points around Rantau Panjang were recorded between March 27 and October 12. Bukit Aman Internal Security and Public Order Department (PGA) Deputy Director Datuk Suzrin Mohamad Rodhi said the damage was believed to have been deliberately done to open up pathways for smuggling activities and cross-border crimes. Suzrin said his team constantly updates field information alongside the National Security Council and the police contingent regarding fence-cutting incidents in the border areas.

items.title: Court grants Perikatan stay on RoS deregistration, allows coalition to contest Melaka state polls
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 22 — The High Court here today allowed Perikatan Nasional’s (PN) application to stay the Registrar of Societies’ (RoS) decision to revoke the coalition’s registration pending the outcome of its judicial review. Judge Datuk Azizan Md Arshad also granted PN’s application to stay the enforcement of an RoS notice suspending all activities of the political coalition. The decision allows PN to continue its political activities, including contesting the Melaka state election scheduled for November 14.

items.title: Iran warns it will hit US bases if Hormuz ship escorts continue
items.summary: TEHRAN, Oct 22 — Iran’s Revolutionary Guards on Thursday threatened to strike American bases across the Middle East if the US military continues to escort ships through the Strait of Hormuz. “The US military must know that if this trend continues, the conflict will extend to its bases in the region,” the Guards, the ideological arm of Iran’s military, said in a statement on their Sepah News website. It regularly attacks ships that attempt to navigate the strait without its authorisation.

items.title: Do Malaysians know MA63? Communications Ministry may run a study to find out
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 22 — The Communications Ministry is considering conducting a dedicated study to gauge public understanding of the Malaysia Agreement 1963 (MA63) and the history of Malaysia’s formation. Deputy Communications Minister Teo Nie Ching said neither the ministry nor its agencies, including the Malaysian Information Department (Japen), had conducted a baseline study for this purpose. “At present, neither RTM nor Japen has conducted a survey to measure public understanding of MA63 and the formation of Malaysia.

items.title: Pay up or go to jail: 43 fined for using other people’s Malaysian ID cards in Johor Bahru
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Oct 22 — A total of 43 individuals, including three Malaysians, were fined between RM1,000 and RM9,000 by three Magistrates’ Courts here today for using forged identity cards or copies of identity cards belonging to other people. Of the total, 35 were charged with using copies of other people’s identity cards, while the remaining eight were charged with using forged identity cards as personal identification documents. The accused, aged between 18 and 49, comprised three Malaysians and foreign nationals from Indonesia and the Philippines.

items.title: MyEG suspension to continue as RM314m outstanding payment remains unsettled, says Loke
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 22 — Transport Minister Anthony Loke Siew Fook today said the outstanding payment MyEG Services Bhd (MyEG) owes the government has yet to be settled, following the suspension of the company’s services as a Road Transport Department (JPJ) collection agent earlier this month. MyEG is a digital and e-government services provider that was previously tasked with collecting JPJ-related payments. He said the suspension had not disrupted public access to JPJ services, as motorists could continue using alternative channels, including the MyJPJ application, to access their information and carry out transactions.

items.title: Haze row: Malaysia to take transboundary pollution to Asean meeting in Manila
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 22 — Malaysia urges Indonesia to take firm and effective action to tackle fires contributing to transboundary haze pollution, which is affecting air quality and public well-being in Malaysia. Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Minister Datuk Seri Arthur Joseph Kurup said Malaysia respected its good diplomatic relations with Indonesia but reserved the right to demand appropriate action to ensure its people could enjoy clean air. “Malaysia’s stance is clear.

items.title: TalentCorp business as usual, says HR Ministry, as it lodges reports on alleged interference
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 22 — The Human Resources Ministry (Kesuma) has lodged several official reports with the authorities over alleged attempts to interfere with an ongoing review and investigation at Talent Corporation Malaysia Berhad (TalentCorp). In a statement today, the ministry said the alleged interference involved spreading misleading information, influencing individuals within the agency, and diverting attention from matters under scrutiny. It said such actions could undermine the integrity and independence of the review and investigation.
